slowed_down_by: `npm install -g @monid-ai/cli` failed with a permissions error on the system prefix; had to set a user npm prefix and add it to PATH before `monid` was available.
Response shapes differ per endpoint (items under data.items / posts / videos, Reddit link in `permalink` vs gallery `url`), so I had to inspect raw JSON before normalising.
YouTube results only carry relative publish times ('1 day ago'); the createdUtc Monid derives from them is day-precision only, so YouTube dates are approximate.

Reddit keyword search returned some posts that only mention the brand deep in the body or not visibly at all (e.g. grocery giveaway, personal diary posts), and TikTok search included a few loosely related videos, so results needed manual filtering.
what_went_well: Setup was quick once installed; `monid discover` found one provider (anyapi) covering X, TikTok, Reddit and YouTube with date filters, all four searches ran in parallel and finished in a few seconds for well under $0.01 total.
